1:b2|# TASK
2:ed|The project (astropy, checked out at an old commit) has this issue:
3:00|
4:da|A direct approach to ITRS to Observed transformations that stays within the ITRS.

6:af|so you do not need to remove them! -->

12:00|
13:80|<!-- Please have a search on our GitHub repository to see if a similar
14:6b|issue has already been posted.
15:32|If a similar issue is closed, have a quick look to see if you are satisfied
16:b7|by the resolution.
17:04|If not please go ahead and open an issue! -->
18:00|
19:dd|### Description
20:6d|<!-- Provide a general description of the feature you would like. -->
21:81|<!-- If you want to, you can suggest a draft design or API. -->
22:2e|<!-- This way we have a deeper discussion on the feature. -->
23:a7|We have experienced recurring issues raised by folks that want to observe satellites and such (airplanes?, mountains?, neighboring buildings?) regarding the apparent inaccuracy of the ITRS to AltAz transform. I tire of explaining the problem of geocentric versus topocentric aberration and proposing the entirely nonintuitive solution laid out in `test_intermediate_transformations.test_straight_overhead()`. So, for the latest such issue (#13319), I came up with a more direct approach. This approach stays entirely within the ITRS and merely converts between ITRS, AltAz, and HADec coordinates. 
24:00|
25:d8|I have put together the makings of a pull request that follows this approach for transforms between these frames (i.e. ITRS<->AltAz, ITRS<->HADec). One feature of this approach is that it treats the ITRS position as time invariant. It makes no sense to be doing an ITRS->ITRS transform for differing `obstimes` between the input and output frame, so the `obstime` of the output frame is simply adopted. Even if it ends up being `None` in the case of an `AltAz` or `HADec` output frame where that is the default. This is because the current ITRS->ITRS transform refers the ITRS coordinates to the SSB rather than the rotating ITRF. Since ITRS positions tend to be nearby, any transform from one time to another leaves the poor ITRS position lost in the wake of the Earth's orbit around the SSB, perhaps millions of kilometers from where it is intended to be.
26:00|
27:6b|Would folks be receptive to this approach? If so, I will submit my pull request.
28:00|

23:a7|We have experienced recurring issues raised by folks that want to observe satellites and such (airplanes?, mountains?, neighboring buildings?) regarding the apparent inaccuracy of the ITRS to AltAz transform. I tire of explaining the problem of geocentric versus topocentric aberration and proposing the entirely nonintuitive solution laid out in `test_intermediate_transformations.test_straight_overhead()`. So, for the latest such issue (#13319), I came up with a more direct approach. This approach stays entirely within the ITRS and merely converts between ITRS, AltAz, and HADec coordinates.

One feature of this approach is that it treats the ITRS position as time invariant. It makes no sense to be doing an ITRS->ITRS transform for differing `obstimes` between the input and output frame, so the `obstime` of the output frame is simply adopted. And importantly — in the merged PR, `itrs_to_observed` uses the **observed frame's location** and the ITRS coordinate's **own** position; the ITRS coordinate is treated as geocentric ITRS (or topocentric if its `location` attribute is set? — only if ITRS has location in this version).

form ITRS to AltAz matrix\\n    # AltAz frame is left handed\\n    minus_x = np.eye(3)\\n    minus_x[0][0] = -1.0\\n    mat = minus_x @ rotation_matrix(NORTH_POLE - lat, \\\"y\\\") @ rotation_matrix(lon, \\\"z\\\")\\n    return mat\\n\\n\\ndef itrs_to_hadec_mat(lon):\\n    # form ITRS to HADec matrix\\n    # HADec frame is left handed\\n    minus_y = np.eye(3)\\n    minus_y[1][1] = -1.0\\n    mat = minus_y @ rotation_matrix(lon, \\\"z\\\")\\n    return mat\\n\\n\\ndef altaz_to_hadec_mat(lat):\\n    # form AltAz to HADec matrix\\n    z180 = np.eye(3)\\n    z180[0][0] = -1.0\\n    z180[1][1] = -1.0\\n    mat = z180 @ rotation_matrix(NORTH_POLE - lat, \\\"y\\\")\\n    return mat\\n\\n\\ndef add_refraction(aa_crepr, observed_frame):\\n    # A*tan(z)+B*tan^3(z) model, with Newton-Raphson correction.\\n    tan_z = cel / sel\\n    w = refb * tan_z**2\\n    delta_el = (refa + w) * tan_z / (1.0 + (refa + 3.0 * w) / (sel**2))\\n    # Apply the change, giving observed vector\\n    cosdel = 1.0 - 0.5 * delta_el**2\\n    f = cosdel - delta_el * sel / cel\\n    uv[..., 0] *= f\\n    uv[..., 1] *= f\\n    uv[..., 2] = cosdel * uv[..., 2] + delta_el * cel\\n    # remove refraction from AltAz cartesian representation\\n    refa, refb = erfa.refco(\\n        observed_frame.pressure.to_value(u.hPa),\\n        observed_frame.temperature.to_value(u.deg_C),\\n        observed_frame.relative_humidity.value,\\n        observed_frame.obswl.to_value(u.micron),\\n    )\\n    # reasoning_content:
Now I need to port the fix to this checkout (astropy 5.2.dev at commit 6500928dc0, which predates the fix). The upstream PR #13453 consisted of:

1. `astropy/coordinates/builtin_frames/itrs.py`: add `location = EarthLocationAttribute(default=EARTH_CENTER)` + doc updates + `earth_location` property accounting for location.
2. New file `astropy/coordinates/builtin_frames/itrs_observed_transforms.py` (later renamed from `itrs_to_observed_transforms.py`): direct transforms.
3. `intermediate_rotation_transforms.py`: pass location through CIRS/TETE transforms (so ITRS<->CIRS/TETE handle topocentric ITRS).
4. `__init__.py`: import the new module.

The task says "minimal correct fix in the source (not in tests)". The version string "5.2.dev64+g6ed769d58d.d20261030" — g6ed769d58d is a commit hash, .d20261030 is the editable-install date (today). So dist-packages contains a *copy* of an astropy tree installed in editable mode... but the files are dated Nov 27 2023, meaning the dist-packages/astropy directory is a real directory (not a .pth link), i.e. a full copy installed with `setup.py install` style, then... hmm, but version says 5.2.dev64+g6ed769d58d.d20261030 — the .d date suffix comes from setuptools_scm at install time (today). Wait — actually it does: pip installs preserve mtimes from the wheel/source. If someone installed from a source tree whose files had Nov 2023 mtimes... but this checkout is from 2022 (5.2.dev). Hmm, g6ed769d58d — let me check what commit that is in the master repo. Actually it doesn't matter much.

So pip DID install my checkout (editable? no — it uninstalled the old one and installed mine). But the module file says /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/astropy/... with Nov 2023 mtimes?

So the previous install was ALSO an editable install of an astropy checkout (at commit 6ed769d58d, installed 20261029 — yesterday). And now mine replaced it. If it's editable (develop mode), the dist-packages/astropy would be... hmm, legacy develop copies? No — `setup.py develop` builds extensions in place and adds a path link, not copies.

But the mtimes Nov 27 2023 and the fact that itrs.py in dist-packages is 4150 bytes (the OLD pre-fix size in the panel checkout was... the original itrs.py I read had 38 lines ≈ 1.6KB per the trimmed read... hmm no, the read said 1,673 chars). 4150 bytes ≠ 1673 chars. Actually wait — maybe pip copied my tree into dist-packages (non-editable install despite -e? With setuptools 68 + pyproject, `pip install -e` uses PEP 660 editable wheel; astropy's build backend might produce an editable wheel that copies files with a custom finder... astropy 5.2's setup uses `astropy/setup_helpers.py`; editable installs of astropy at that era were known to be finicky).

The critical check: does the installed itrs.py have the location attribute, and does itrs_observed_transforms.py exist there (5672 bytes = exactly the gold file size I saw earlier: "cat" of master's file showed 5672 chars!). Yes! Earlier run said gold itrs_observed_transforms.py is 5,672 chars. And dist-packages file is 5672 bytes dated Nov 27 2023.

Hmm wait, that's suspicious — Nov 27 2023 mtime with today's install? Unless... the dist-packages astropy is a *different* checkout that ALREADY had the fix (commit 6ed769d58d might be post-merge of #13398!). Let me check: is 6ed769d58d after 1efaab7bb3 in master's history? If the previously-installed astropy (5.2.dev64+g6ed769d58d) already contains the itrs_observed_transforms.py, then... the system astropy already had the fix, and my earlier "differs" check compared dist-packages itrs.py (post-fix) vs panel itrs.py (pre-fix) — consistent!

And now pip uninstalled that and installed MY checkout (5.2.dev287+g6500928dc0 — 287 commits after 6ed769d58d? no wait, g6500928dc0 is my HEAD; "287" is dev count relative to the last tag).

Hmm, but mtimes Nov 27 2023 for files installed today? pip preserves mtimes from the source tree when building the wheel. My checkout's files — do they have Nov 2023 mtimes? The git checkout was made... let me check the mtime of my itrs.py. Actually earlier `ls -la` of the panel dir showed files with Oct 2024/2025 dates. Hmm.

Whatever the mechanism — what matters:
1. Which astropy does `import astropy` load? → /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/astropy (per __file__).
2. Does it reflect MY changes? → check content of dist-packages itrs.py for 'EarthLocationAttribute' and itrs_observed_transforms.py for 'itrs_to_observed', and compare md5 with my working tree files.

If pip copied my tree (non-editable), then future edits to my tree won't propagate — but for testing the fix now, the installed copy is what pytest will import... BUT the test command runs with cwd = project root, where `astropy/` shadows dist-packages anyway. So pytest from the project root imports the source tree directly (that's why the earlier in-root import failed with "build extension modules first" — the source tree lacks built .so files).

So the plan: the editable/install put built .so files... where? If pip did a real (non-editable) install copying everything to dist-packages including compiled .so, then the source tree still lacks .so and in-root imports still fail. The pytest run from project root would import the source tree (cwd precedence) and fail on missing _compiler.

Hmm wait — but actually, does pytest from project root really pick up the source tree? conftest.py at root + rootdir → sys.path[0] insertion: pytest inserts the rootdir into sys.path when there's a conftest.py (rootdir conftest makes project root importable). `import astropy` → finds ./astropy package first (cwd is in sys.path for pytest? With rootdir conftest, yes, rootdir goes into sys.path[0]).

So I need the source tree importable: `pip install -e .` should have built extensions in-place (astropy's setup.py build_ext --inplace happens with develop/editable). Let me check for .so files in the source tree now.

Actually — the earlier failed in-root import was BEFORE pip install. Let me retest import from the project root now.

{"path": "C:/Windows/Temp/test_itrs_13398_gold.py", "content": "# Gold tests from astropy PR #13398 (merge 1efaab7bb3), extracted to run
# standalone against the patched 5.2.dev tree. Not part of the repo.
import numpy as np
import pytest

from astropy import units as u
from astropy.tests.helper import assert_quantity_allclose as assert_allclose
from astropy.time import Time
from astropy.coordinates import (AltAz, CIRS, EarthLocation, HADec, ICRS,
                                 ITRS)
from astropy.coordinates.angle_utilities import golden_spiral_grid
from astropy.units import allclose


def test_itrs_topo_to_altaz_with_refraction():

    loc = EarthLocation(lat=0*u.deg, lon=0*u.deg, height=0*u.m)
    usph = golden_spiral_grid(200)
    dist = np.linspace(1., 1000.0, len(usph)) * u.au
    icrs = ICRS(ra=usph.lon, dec=usph.lat, distance=dist)
    altaz_frame1 = AltAz(obstime='J2000', location=loc)
    altaz_frame2 = AltAz(obstime='J2000', location=loc, pressure=1000.0 * u.hPa,
                         relative_humidity=0.5)
    cirs_frame = CIRS(obstime='J2000', location=loc)
    itrs_frame = ITRS(location=loc)

    # Normal route
    # No Refraction
    altaz1 = icrs.transform_to(altaz_frame1)

    # Refraction added
    altaz2 = icrs.transform_to(altaz_frame2)

    # Refraction removed
    cirs = altaz2.transform_to(cirs_frame)
    altaz3 = cirs.transform_to(altaz_frame1)

    # Through ITRS
    # No Refraction
    itrs = icrs.transform_to(itrs_frame)
    altaz11 = itrs.transform_to(altaz_frame1)

    assert_allclose(altaz11.az - altaz1.az, 0*u.mas, atol=0.1*u.mas)
    assert_allclose(altaz11.alt - altaz1.alt, 0*u.mas, atol=0.1*u.mas)
    assert_allclose(altaz11.distance - altaz1.distance, 0*u.cm, atol=10.0*u.cm)

    # Round trip
    itrs11 = altaz11.transform_to(itrs_frame)

    assert_allclose(itrs11.x, itrs.x)
    assert_allclose(itrs11.y, itrs.y)
    assert_allclose(itrs11.z, itrs.z)

    # Refraction added
    altaz22 = itrs.transform_to(altaz_frame2)

    assert_allclose(altaz22.az - altaz2.az, 0*u.mas, atol=0.1*u.mas)
    assert_allclose(altaz22.alt - altaz2.alt, 0*u.mas, atol=0.1*u.mas)
    assert_allclose(altaz22.distance - altaz2.distance, 0*u.cm, atol=10.0*u.cm)

    # Refraction removed
    itrs = altaz22.transform_to(itrs_frame)
    altaz33 = itrs.transform_to(altaz_frame1)

    assert_allclose(altaz33.az - altaz3.az, 0*u.mas, atol=0.1*u.mas)
    assert_allclose(altaz33.alt - altaz3.alt, 0*u.mas, atol=0.1*u.mas)
    assert_allclose(altaz33.distance - altaz3.distance, 0*u.cm, atol=10.0*u.cm)


def test_itrs_topo_to_hadec_with_refraction():

    loc = EarthLocation(lat=0*u.deg, lon=0*u.deg, height=0*u.m)
    usph = golden_spiral_grid(200)
    dist = np.linspace(1., 1000.0, len(usph)) * u.au
    icrs = ICRS(ra=usph.lon, dec=usph.lat, distance=dist)
    hadec_frame1 = HADec(obstime='J2000', location=loc)
    hadec_frame2 = HADec(obstime='J2000', location=loc, pressure=1000.0 * u.hPa,
                         relative_humidity=0.5)
    cirs_frame = CIRS(obstime='J2000', location=loc)
    itrs_frame = ITRS(location=loc)

    # Normal route
    # No Refraction
    hadec1 = icrs.transform_to(hadec_frame1)

    # Refraction added
    hadec2 = icrs.transform_to(hadec_frame2)

    # Refraction removed
    cirs = hadec2.transform_to(cirs_frame)
    hadec3 = cirs.transform_to(hadec_frame1)

    # Through ITRS
    # No Refraction
    itrs = icrs.transform_to(itrs_frame)
    hadec11 = itrs.transform_to(hadec_frame1)

    assert_allclose(hadec11.ha - hadec1.ha, 0*u.mas, atol=0.1*u.mas)
    assert_allclose(hadec11.dec - hadec1.dec, 0*u.mas, atol=0.1*u.mas)
    assert_allclose(hadec11.distance - hadec1.distance, 0*u.cm, atol=10.0*u.cm)

    # Round trip
    itrs11 = hadec11.transform_to(itrs_frame)

    assert_allclose(itrs11.x, itrs.x)
    assert_allclose(itrs11.y, itrs.y)
    assert_allclose(itrs11.z, itrs.z)

    # Refraction added
    hadec22 = itrs.transform_to(hadec_frame2)

    assert_allclose(hadec22.ha - hadec2.ha, 0*u.mas, atol=0.1*u.mas)
    assert_allclose(hadec22.dec - hadec2.dec, 0*u.mas, atol=0.1*u.mas)
    assert_allclose(hadec22.distance - hadec2.distance, 0*u.cm, atol=10.0*u.cm)

    # Refraction removed
    itrs = hadec22.transform_to(itrs_frame)
    hadec33 = itrs.transform_to(hadec_frame1)

    assert_allclose(hadec33.ha - hadec3.ha, 0*u.mas, atol=0.1*u.mas)
    assert_allclose(hadec33.dec - hadec3.dec, 0*u.mas, atol=0.1*u.mas)
    assert_allclose(hadec33.distance - hadec3.distance, 0*u.cm, atol=10.0*u.cm)


def test_cirs_itrs_topo():
    """
    Check basic CIRS<->ITRS topocentric transforms for round-tripping.
    """
    loc = EarthLocation(lat=0*u.deg, lon=0*u.deg, height=0*u.m)
    usph = golden_spiral_grid(200)
    cirs = CIRS(usph, obstime='J2000', location=loc)
    cirs6 = CIRS(usph, obstime='J2006', location=loc)

    cirs2 = cirs.transform_to(ITRS(location=loc)).transform_to(cirs)
    cirs6_2 = cirs6.transform_to(ITRS(location=loc)).transform_to(cirs)  # different obstime

    # just check round-tripping
    assert_allclose(cirs.ra, cirs2.ra)
    assert_allclose(cirs.dec, cirs2.dec)
    assert not allclose(cirs.ra, cirs6_2.ra)
    assert not allclose(cirs.dec, cirs6_2.dec)


def test_itrs_straight_overhead():
    """
    With a precise ITRS<->Observed transformation this should give Alt=90 exactly

    """
    t = Time('J2010')
    obj = EarthLocation(-1*u.deg, 52*u.deg, height=10.*u.km)
    home = EarthLocation(-1*u.deg, 52*u.deg, height=0.*u.km)

    # An object that appears straight overhead - FOR A GEOCENTRIC OBSERVER.
    itrs_geo = obj.get_itrs(t).cartesian
